truthBoundary: Observed facts are source-backed snapshots. Product implications are hypotheses requiring country- and segment-level validation. No research signal has production authority.

signals.title: Digital life is widespread, mobile-led, multi-platform and increasingly AI-assisted

notes: Global signal is stored with GLOBAL_PROXY; it must never be interpreted as a Europe-only finding.

evidence.title: Digital 2026 Mid-Year Global Update
evidence.claim: 6.12B internet users, 5.79B social-media identities and about 2.42B active GenAI users were reported in April 2026; mobile phones are used to access the internet by the overwhelming majority of internet users.

evidence.title: Digital 2026 Global Overview
evidence.claim: Adult social users commonly use multiple platforms and cite several distinct reasons for social-platform use; keeping in touch remains the top global motivation.

signals.hypothesis: A continuous Personal AI plus unified communication, social, files, learning, work, marketplace and media experience can reduce app fragmentation if permissions and boundaries stay explicit.

signals.title: Africa combines fast digital growth with affordability and usage barriers

notes: Country-level variation is large; do not generalize the continental profile to an individual user.

evidence.title: The Mobile Economy Africa 2026
evidence.claim: GSMA reports strong mobile-led economic growth while identifying affordability as a key barrier to digital inclusion.

evidence.title: Digital 2026 Nigeria
evidence.claim: Nigeria provides an example of substantial mobile connectivity alongside a much lower share of the total population using the internet and social media.

signals.hypothesis: Pantavion should treat low-data, offline-capable, local-language and trust-preserving operation as first-class product modes rather than degraded afterthoughts.

signals.title: Asia-Pacific is scaling 5G and AI while digital trust becomes a core requirement

notes: Asia is too diverse for a single platform model; country/language ecosystems must remain distinct.

evidence.title: The Mobile Economy Asia Pacific 2026
evidence.claim: GSMA projects 1.5B 5G connections in Asia Pacific by 2030 and identifies AI integration and proactive digital trust/scam reduction as strategic priorities.

evidence.title: Digital 2026 Japan
evidence.claim: Japan illustrates high internet and social-platform adoption in a mature Asian digital market.

signals.hypothesis: The strongest Pantavion fit is a multilingual, high-scale Personal AI and communication layer that can connect social, commerce, files and services while aggressively reducing scams and impersonation.

signals.title: Europe is highly connected and demands resilient cross-border digital services

evidence.title: The Mobile Economy Europe 2026
evidence.claim: The EU has roughly 370M unique mobile internet users, more than 80% of the regional population, and mobile networks support a growing range of services.

signals.hypothesis: Pantavion can differentiate through transparent privacy, multilingual cross-border continuity, interoperability and clear user control rather than attention-maximizing design.

signals.title: North America combines very high connectivity with broad social and AI-ready workflows

evidence.title: Digital 2026 United States
evidence.claim: US internet penetration was reported at 93.1%, with 254M social-media user identities.

evidence.title: Digital 2026 Canada
evidence.claim: Canada internet penetration was reported at 95.1%, with social-media identities equivalent to 82.1% of the population.

signals.hypothesis: A strong North American proposition is one Personal AI that moves between personal, creator, professional, communication, media and marketplace workflows without forcing users into separate products.

signals.title: Latin America is mobile-led, socially connected and still constrained by a substantial usage gap

evidence.title: The Mobile Economy Latin America 2026
evidence.claim: GSMA reports a 32% mobile-internet usage gap, expanding 5G adoption, growing AI use and digital trust as a core regional priority.

signals.hypothesis: Pantavion should connect messaging, social discovery, local business, marketplace and AI assistance in a mobile-first experience that remains useful on constrained connections.

signals.title: Oceania combines high adoption in Australia and New Zealand with remote-connectivity realities

evidence.title: Digital 2026 Australia
evidence.claim: Australia had social-media user identities equivalent to 77.7% of its population.

evidence.title: Digital 2026 New Zealand
evidence.claim: New Zealand internet penetration was reported at 96.2%, with social-media identities equivalent to 80.6% of the population.

signals.hypothesis: Pantavion should combine mainstream high-connectivity experiences with robust remote, travel, emergency and delayed-sync modes for dispersed communities and field contexts.

signals.title: Antarctica is an extreme operational edge case rather than a conventional consumer market

notes: Treat Antarctica as a resilience/science/field-operations proving ground, not a consumer-demand proxy.

evidence.title: Connecting the last continent
evidence.claim: US Antarctic stations and field camps rely on satellite internet; capacity limitations can require bandwidth rationing, motivating study of more resilient connectivity.

evidence.title: Australian Antarctic research stations and field locations
evidence.claim: Australia operates permanent and seasonal research locations where scientific and operational workflows must function in remote conditions.

signals.hypothesis: If Pantavion works safely under Antarctic-style intermittent connectivity, it gains resilience patterns useful for disaster zones, ships, remote communities and infrastructure teams worldwide.
proposedCapabilities: satellite and radio aware fallback orchestration
